note: The crew doctor's checks for the walk brief. The team chose the order (before, during, after) and the checks; each one is a check NASA publishes, with NASA's value and its source. 'compare' names the forecast value the map sets beside the check (see doctorChecks in js/brief.js); null means the map has no forecast for it. Sources read 14 Nov 2026.

before.check: The crew doctor clears the walker for this walk.
Aerobic fitness is high enough for walking on a planet's surface.
before.nasa: Maximal oxygen uptake at or above 36.5 ml/min/kg [V1 4002].

before.check: The oxygen prebreathe is complete, and any break in it is logged.
before.nasa: The protocol must keep the chance of decompression sickness under 4% [V2 6008]. On the space station it is 4 hours on pure oxygen in the suit.

sources.label: NASA technical brief OCHMO-TB-037 Rev D, Decompression Sickness

before.nasa: At least 240 mL of water for each hour in the suit [V2 11030].

during.check: Stored body heat stays inside NASA's range.
The work rate is measured, from heart rate, and shown to the walker.
during.nasa: The suit system must measure or calculate metabolic rate and display it [V2 11037], [V2 11038].

sources.label: NASA NTRS 20210024317, metabolic rate estimated from heart rate

during.check: Carbon dioxide in the helmet stays low.
during.nasa: Up to 4.0 mmHg with no time limit; never above 15.0 mmHg [V2 11039].

during.check: The walker stays within reach of shelter.
during.nasa: NASA's plan for Moon walks: within a one-hour walk back, and up to 2 km from the lander (sections 9.6 and 4.2.1.3.1).

sources.label: NASA Exploration EVA System Concept of Operations, EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B

during.check: If the radio link is lost: change position, try the other radio, then end the walk and return.

sources.label: NASA Exploration EVA System Concept of Operations, EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B

after.check: Hands, fingernails and shoulders are examined.
after.nasa: Hand and finger injuries are the most common spacewalk injuries; shoulder injuries are among the most serious.

sources.label: NASA evidence report, Risk of Injury and Compromised Performance due to EVA Operations (2021), NTRS 20220004017

after.check: Body mass is compared with the value before the walk, to find the water lost.
after.nasa: Losing 2.5% of body weight as water lowers performance.

sources.label: NASA technical brief OCHMO-TB-027 Rev B, Water

after.check: The radiation dosimeter is read and the dose is logged.
after.nasa: Each crew member's dosimeter logs exposure through the mission. Career limit: 600 mSv [V1 4030].

after.check: Eyes, nose and hands are checked for dust, and dust in the habitat air is measured.
after.nasa: Martian dust finer than 10 µm in habitat air: under 0.1 mg/m³ as a time-weighted average [V2 6253]. Lunar dust caused eye irritation that needed rinsing.

sources.label: NASA technical brief OCHMO-TB-011 Rev B, Lunar Dust
